pairs.question: Quid ergo profecit quod protulit fastos?
pairs.answer: Occultatam putant quodam tempore istam tabulam, ut dies agendi peterentur a paucis.
pairs.derivation: Cicero discusses Cn. Flavius and his publication of the fasti, then poses his own question 'quid ergo profecit quod protulit fastos?' and answers it: the calendar-tablet had previously been kept hidden so that court-days could be sought from only a few. Answer ends at the first full stop, before 'nec vero pauci sunt auctores...' which turns to defending the historical attribution. Only the first word's capitalization normalized; no scaffolding present in span.

pairs.question: Vnde me iubes petere cibaria praefecti?
pairs.answer: Me non instituisse iis dare cibaria quorum opera non essem usus.
pairs.derivation: Gavius accosts Cicero and asks 'Unde me iubes petere cibaria praefecti?'; Cicero answers. Dropped the speech tag/narration 'respondi lenius quam putabant oportuisse qui aderant' (= 'I replied more mildly than the bystanders thought proper') as framing, leaving the operative answering clause beginning 'me non instituisse...'. Answer ends before 'abiit iratus' (narration). First word capitalization normalized; the garbled '<ut&t;' artifact lies in the framing before the quote, not in the extracted span.
